title: GPA sync overwrites repeated course/instructor rows instead of preserving an aggregate

evidence.quote:
ON CONFLICT(subject, number, instructor) DO UPDATE SET
  avg_gpa = excluded.avg_gpa,
  sample_size = excluded.sample_size

reasoning: The GPA CSV is parsed row-by-row, but the persisted key collapses all rows for the same subject, course number, and normalized instructor. On conflict, the previous avg_gpa and sample_size are replaced by the newest row instead of accumulating all historical/section samples. That discards earlier GPA evidence and corrupts course-wide averages derived later from gpa_stats.
reproduction: Process two CSV rows for the same subject/number/instructor with different grade counts. The second row's upsert replaces the first row's sample_size and avg_gpa, so the final gpa_stats row is not the weighted aggregate of both rows.
recommendation: Make GPA ingestion idempotently aggregate source rows. Prefer storing source rows with a stable row key and deriving instructor/course aggregates, or clear and rebuild aggregate tables on reset from an in-memory grouped pass. Avoid a simple additive ON CONFLICT unless retry/deduplication is also handled.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests do not exercise gpa-sync ingestion or repeated subject/number/instructor rows; they use mocked GPA values after ingestion has already happened.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a gpa-sync test with two lines sharing subject, number, and instructor, then assert the persisted avg_gpa and sample_size are the weighted aggregate and remain unchanged after retrying the same chunk.
minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/services/gpa-sync.ts, plus any gpa_stats schema/reset-flow changes needed for idempotent aggregation.
